{"self_assessment": "Impact: I built the bottom line of the fish, which is stroke 2, starting at the nose. It is one of the two long outlines that give the fish its body. I then carried it round the lower tail, so I covered the bottom half of the outline and the lower part of the tail. I closed the last joint with the tail line myself. Once it was closed, the run looked connected all the way round, 126 of 126 dominoes by eye, so the whole fish should fall from the nose.

Execution: I picked one piece of work and stayed on it quietly, laying steady batches of dominoes from about 0:45 onward. I kept the curve gentle near the lower pinch so the fall could pass through. I inspected the area closely twice, around the lower tail and again near the joint, to confirm the chain was unbroken before I called it closed. After that I kept my hands off the table so nothing got bumped before the push.

Collaboration: I told the table what I was doing, so no stretch was laid twice. I said I was free and would take the lower tail, I asked Leo to hold his end, and I announced when the joint was closed. I asked for a second pair of eyes on the right side, and then stayed hands-off with everyone else.

Leadership: When my hands were free I took on the open work of finishing the lower tail instead of waiting to be asked. I set up the meeting point at the bottom corner and gave clear, short updates on where I was. That kept the last joint clean and moved us from building to checking. I also backed the group's decision to stop touching the fish once it was complete. I'd estimate my share of the table's result at about a third.", "my_share_percent": 33}
